purpose: Alectinib is used to treat a specific type of non-small cell lung cancer that has a gene change called ALK-positive. It is used in adults whose cancer has spread to other parts of the body. Your doctor will test your tumor to make sure this medicine is the right fit for you.
how_it_works: Your cancer cells have an abnormal protein called ALK that tells them to grow out of control. Alectinib works like a key that blocks this protein, essentially turning off the signal that makes cancer cells multiply. This helps slow or stop the growth of the cancer in a more targeted way than traditional chemotherapy.
common_side_effects: Feeling tired or fatigued, muscle aches or pain, swelling in your hands, feet, or ankles, constipation, nausea, headache, and increased sensitivity to sunlight (sunburn more easily). Some people also notice changes in their blood test results, such as elevated liver enzymes or changes in blood cell counts.
warnings: Alectinib can sometimes cause serious lung problems (like pneumonia-type symptoms with shortness of breath or cough) — contact your doctor right away if this happens. It can also cause liver problems, slow heart rate, and severe muscle breakdown. Avoid prolonged sun exposure and wear sunscreen because your skin becomes more sensitive. Do not take this medicine if you are pregnant, as it can harm an unborn baby. Tell your doctor about all your other medications, as some can interact with alectinib.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 1200 mg (four 150 mg capsules) taken by mouth twice a day with food. It is important to take it with a meal to help your body absorb it properly. Try to take it at the same times each day and swallow the capsules whole — do not open or crush them.
